The new `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly writes `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` as a placeholder when sync mode is enabled and the sync response lacks it, and the new `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a sync-endpoint response containing only access token/expiry. judged_text: Salesforce is the only refreshed app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens: it performs a hardcoded direct fetch using `credentialKey.refresh_token`, which in sync mode is either absent or the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" written by parseRefreshTokenResponse. With credential sync enabled, every Salesforce refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" to login.salesforce.com, fails, and throws — Salesforce calendar sync is completely broken under the exact configuration this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh is implemented via a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using `credentialKey.refresh_token` and is not routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens` abstraction that other OAuth apps were updated to use. Under the PR’s new “credential sync” mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the shared refresh flow is designed to work even when `refresh_token` is missing by using `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to tolerate minimal responses and even writing a placeholder `refresh_token` string when absent. Because Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, it will still attempt to refresh against Salesforce using whatever is stored in `credential.key.refresh_token` (which, in sync mode, can be missing or become the placeholder), causing refresh to fail and the code to throw (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`). This breaks Salesforce refresh behavior under the configuration this PR introduces.
